captures.q: What is “Undoing the Suppression: The Counter-Stack — Inseparability Engineering from Detection to Custody” by Lee Sharks, and how does it work? Ground your answer in the document itself.
captures.description: THE TEXT CALLED INACCESSIBLE TWICE; THE STACK RECONSTRUCTED FROM ITS NEIGHBOURS: asked what Undoing the Suppression: The Counter-Stack is and how it works, ChatGPT finds the archive listing (Datasets at Hugging Face; Research Papers), identifies deposit 1497, its date and its collection, and reports 'the full-text page was not accessible through the available retrieval results'; it gives four generic stages (detection, verification, provenance, custody), marked 'not … a verified, section-by-section summary', and asks for the text. After an operator turn blank in the paste ('You were right to push back'), it finds the blog mirror of 19 August and rebuilds the stack from the surrounding records: the Suppression Map (#1496) with structure, material, attribution and operator-legibility; reception edges and the operator registry; the build record's corpus deposits and their repair; custody that keeps dead identifiers visible. It ends 'I cannot honestly claim to have read the entire body of deposit 1497.' The paper's six layers (detection, relation, operator registry, surfaces, custody, controller) and its thesis — 'Suppression worked by SEPARABILITY', answered by inseparability engineering — are not reached; the answer's gloss of inseparability, from the title, lands near it.
